passageLocation.openingWords: That was a memorable day to me

text: That was a memorable day to me, for it made great changes in me. But it is the same with any life. Imagine one selected day struck out of it, and think how different its course would have been. Pause you who read this, and think for a moment of the long chain of iron or gold, of thorns or flowers, that would never have bound you, but for the formation of the first link on one memorable day.

curation.context: In Chapter IX of Dickens’s 1861 novel, Pip looks back on a day that altered the course of his life.
curation.rationale: A single day becomes a chain of iron or gold, thorns or flowers. The balanced images and direct invitation to pause support poems about memory, consequence, chance and binding.
